notes: What the app gets wrong today. Each entry prints as KNOWN on every run and does not fail it. An entry that stops matching fails the run until it is taken off the list, so a fix is always noticed. The contrast entries are one per screen, theme and color pair, each with the ratio the app draws. The language entries are one per kind of word the API cannot send in Spanish yet, which stay until it does, and one per place the portal itself still draws English, which the build that fixes it takes off. The checklist entries are what the Tasks screen cannot do yet, which the next commit takes off.

accepted.why: The person's name in the header runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis when there is no room. Accepted: the name is theirs to recognise at a glance, the avatar beside it is the way to their profile, and the whole name is on the Profile screen.
The role under the name runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis the same way, and for the same reason.

An unfinished report's title on Help runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis when there is no room, the way a name does. The stub serves the first form's title in Spanish from this build on, and the Spanish is longer.
The role under the name, in Spanish now, runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis the same way the English one does, and for the same reason.

failures.what: is a to-do item the API sent in English
failures.why: A to-do item and its instructions are written in English in the database and the API sends them as written. The API's build gives them Spanish and sends the language the request asks for.

failures.what: is a to-do zone the API sent in English
failures.why: A to-do item's zone is written in English in the database and sent as written, the same as the item.

failures.what: is a supply the API sent in English
failures.why: A supply's name and its unit are written in English in the database and sent as written.

failures.what: is a notice the API sent in English
failures.why: An in-app notice is written by the API in English at the moment it is sent. The API's build writes it in the person's saved language.

failures.what: is an inspection item the API sent in English
failures.why: An inspection's name, its items and their zones are written in English in the database and sent as written.

failures.what: is a service the API sent in English
failures.why: A shift's service is written in English in the database and sent as written.

failures.what: is a site role the API sent in English
failures.why: A person's role at a site is typed by an admin, in English today, and sent as typed.

failures.what: is a shift name the API sent in English
failures.why: A shift's name is typed by an admin, in English today, and sent as typed.

failures.what: is a Help reply the API sent in English
failures.why: Help's replies, the fixed ones included, arrive from the API in English. The route already carries the language; the reply's language is the API's to change.

failures.what: is a refusal the API sent in English
failures.why: The API's refusals are English sentences on every route but the seven calls made before signing in, which Step 113 answers in the language the request asks for. The portal draws a refusal in Spanish when the table holds that exact sentence and every other one as sent, so a refusal from any other route stays English until the API sends the person's language there too.
The sign out line under Set your PIN is a bare text button, about 20 pixels tall at the standard size. The case drew Home behind it until this build, so the suite never measured it.
The same button, in Spanish.
The service on an open shift, muted text on its chip. 4.46 to 1 against the 4.5 to 1 small text needs. The stub serves a service on its open shift from this build on.
Blue on light mode's blue wash, the badge of a shift someone dropped. 2.49 to 1 against the 4.5 to 1 small text needs. The stub's open shift carries a real origin code from this build on.

failures.where: The whole site's checklist for a person linked to nothing: every item, building and floor hiding none, the count, and a check that holds
failures.check: a person linked to nothing asks for the whole site, with no user_id
failures.why: The Tasks screen asks with ?user_id= for everyone, and the API answers that with only the items linked to the person. Nothing writes a link when a person joins a site or an item is added, and four of six sites have none. The next commit asks for the whole site unless the status says the person has links of their own.

failures.check: the checklist never asks by building or floor
failures.why: The request carries the open shift's building and floor, which the API matches exactly, so an item with no building or no floor drops out of the list. The next commit stops sending both and groups by them on the screen instead.
